transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thank you. I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been having these doubts that are getting hard to shake. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll check something—like a mortgage payment number, or a clause in a client proof, or whether a door is latched—and even after I’ve checked, the thought comes right back, like, what if I missed the one thing that ruins everything?  

I know that probably sounds excessive, but it feels very real in the moment.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these doubts?

Yes… I do, though I try not to make a big production of it. I’ll reopen files or reread emails, sometimes more than once, just to make sure I didn’t miss something. With payments, I’ll check the online confirmation again, even if I know I already saw it.

And sometimes I sort of… say the figures silently in my head until they feel settled, if that makes sense. It’s embarrassing, because a simple invoice or a logo revision can turn into hours that I can’t really bill for. I know it’s not the most efficient way to work.
Do you ever repeat these actions to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to overstate it, but when I reopen a file or reread an email, it’s usually because I’m worried something bad will happen if I don’t—like I’ll miss a payment detail, or send a client proof with some awful mistake in it.

So I’ll check the online payment confirmation again, or go back through the same figures in my head until they feel… settled, I guess. It’s not very rational, I know. But in the moment it feels like if I don’t do it, I’m being careless, and something could go wrong because of me.
Do you feel less anxious after you've completed one of these repetitive checks?

Yes… usually I do feel a little less anxious once I’ve done it. Not completely, exactly, but enough that I feel like I can breathe for a minute.

So I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the payment confirmation again, or sort of repeat the figures silently in my head until they feel “settled.” I know that probably sounds a bit much… and I don’t mean that I’m doing nothing all day, but it can make a simple invoice or logo revision stretch into hours I really can’t bill for.
Are you trying to prevent something specific from happening when you repeat these checks?

Yes… I suppose I am. It’s usually not some dramatic thing, more like I’m trying to stop myself from missing something important.

Like, I’ll reopen the file or reread an email because I’m afraid there’s an error sitting there that I should have caught. Or with payments, I’ll check the online confirmation again so I don’t feel like I’ve messed up the details somehow. And sometimes I’ll repeat the figures silently in my head until they feel… settled.

I know that probably sounds excessive. It can turn something simple, like an invoice or a logo revision, into hours I can’t really bill for. But in the moment it feels like I’m just being responsible, if that makes sense.
Are you ever worried about contamination or harm to yourself or others when you're checking things repeatedly?

Not contamination, no… at least I don’t think that’s really what it is.

The “harm” part is more indirect, I suppose. I get these awful doubts that I’ve missed something important—like a number on the mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof, or even whether a door was properly latched. And even when I know I checked it, the thought comes back like, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything?

I know that sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. I don’t mean I’m expecting some disaster every minute, but the worry feels very real in the moment. Like if I don’t check again, I’m being irresponsible. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like things need to be done in a specific way or order to feel right?

Yes… I think so, though I wouldn’t say it’s a ritual exactly. It’s more that things have to feel finished in the right way.

Like if I reopen a file, I don’t just glance at it—I’ll reread parts of it, then maybe check the email again, or the online payment confirmation, and sometimes I’ll say the figures silently in my head until they feel… settled, I guess. If I don’t do it that way, I keep feeling like something is off.

I know that probably sounds more rigid than I mean it to. It’s not that I want to be difficult or waste time. It just can turn something simple, like an invoice or a logo revision, into hours I can’t really bill for. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel like things need to be symmetrical or exact in any way when you're checking them?

Not really symmetrical, no. It’s not like things have to be lined up or even, exactly.

It’s more… exact in the sense that I need the information to feel right. I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation again, and sometimes repeat the figures silently in my head until they feel settled. I know that sounds like a lot for something simple, but if I don’t do it, I feel like I haven’t finished properly.

And then a small thing, like an invoice or a logo revision, can take hours I can’t really bill for. I’m not proud of that, but… that’s more what it’s like. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're trying to achieve a sense of certainty or reassurance when you repeat these checks?

Yes… I think that’s probably right. I’m not trying to make it into a big thing, but it does feel like I’m chasing that “okay, now I’m sure” feeling.

I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the payment confirmation again, and sometimes repeat the numbers in my head until they feel settled. It’s embarrassing, because it can make something simple—like an invoice or a logo revision—take hours, and I can’t really bill for that.

But in the moment it feels like if I don’t do it, I haven’t been careful enough. Is that what you mean by reassurance?
Do you feel like you have to be in control of these checks to feel okay about them?

Yes… I think so. Maybe “control” is the right word, though I don’t like how that sounds.

It’s more like I need to do the checking myself, in my own way, or it doesn’t feel quite okay. I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, look at the online payment confirmation again, and sometimes repeat the figures quietly in my head until they feel settled.

I know it’s not very efficient. I try to tell myself it’s just being careful, but honestly it can turn something simple, like an invoice or a logo revision, into hours I can’t really bill for. I’m not trying to be excessive… it just doesn’t feel finished unless I’ve checked it that way.
Do you feel like you need to physically perform these checks, like reopening a file or rereading an email, or could you also get reassurance from just thinking through the information in your head?

It’s both, I think. I mean, the physical checking is definitely a big part of it — reopening the file, rereading the email, checking the payment confirmation again. That feels more… solid, I guess.

But I also do it in my head. Like I’ll say the figures silently to myself a few times until they feel settled. I know that probably sounds unnecessary, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yes, it can go back and forth between actually checking and mentally checking.

And that’s when something simple, like an invoice or a logo revision, can stretch into hours I can’t really bill for. I’m trying to answer that clearly — is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are more about avoiding mistakes or making sure everything is perfect?

I’d like to say it’s just about avoiding mistakes, because that sounds reasonable, doesn’t it? I mean, in my work details matter.

But honestly… it’s more this awful doubt that comes in, like I’ve missed something important. A number on a mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof, or even whether a door is properly latched. And even when I know I checked it, the thought comes back like, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?”

So I don’t know if I’d call it perfection exactly. It’s more like I’m trying to stop that fear that I’ve overlooked the one thing that really matters. Does that make sense?
Do you think your need to repeatedly check things is more about ensuring everything is perfect or about avoiding making any mistakes?

I think… more avoiding mistakes, really. Or avoiding that feeling that I’ve missed something important.

Perfection sounds almost like I’m trying to make everything beautiful or flawless, and I don’t think that’s quite it. It’s more that an awful doubt comes in — like, what if I got a number wrong on the mortgage payment, or missed a clause in a client proof, or didn’t latch a door properly — and even if I know I already checked, the thought sort of barges back in.

It’s like, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, I know. But that’s the feeling I’m trying to quiet down. Is that answering it the way you mean?
When you repeat these checks, is it more because you're afraid of making a mistake or because you want to make sure everything is just right?

I think it’s more the fear of making a mistake, honestly. Not so much wanting it to be “just right” in a perfect way.

It’s those doubts that keep coming back — like maybe I missed a number on the mortgage payment, or missed something in a client proof, or didn’t latch a door properly. Even if I know I checked, the thought sort of barges back in, like, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything?

That sounds a bit dramatic when I say it, I know. But that’s more what I’m trying to quiet down. Does that make sense?
When you feel the need to repeat these checks, is it primarily because you are afraid of what might happen if you make a mistake?

Yes… I think that’s right. It’s mostly fear of what could happen if I got something wrong.

I know some of the things sound ordinary — like a number on the mortgage payment, or a line in a client proof, or whether the door is latched — but then this doubt comes back even after I’ve checked. It’s like my mind says, “What if this is the one mistake that causes a serious problem?”

I’m not trying to be difficult or overly fussy, I don’t think. I’m just trying to get rid of that awful feeling that I’ve missed something important. Does that make sense?
When you repeat these checks, is it more about preventing a specific bad outcome from happening or making sure things are done in a very specific way?

I think it’s more about preventing something bad from happening, yes… though sometimes it gets mixed up with needing it to feel settled, if that makes sense.

Like with work, I’ll reopen files more than once, reread emails, check the online payment confirmation again. And I might sort of say the figures silently in my head until they feel… okay, or settled. I’m a little embarrassed saying that.

It’s not that I need to do it in some exact special way, I don’t think. It’s more that I’m afraid I’ve missed something, and then I keep checking until the feeling quiets down. Sometimes a simple invoice or logo revision can take hours, which is frustrating because I can’t really bill for all of that. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
When you repeat these checks, is it primarily because you are afraid of what might happen if you make a mistake or because you want everything to be perfect?

It’s mostly the fear of what could happen if I made a mistake, I think. Not so much that I need everything to be perfect for perfection’s sake.

What brings me in is more these awful doubts — like I’ve missed something important, a number on the mortgage payment, a clause in a client proof, or even whether a door was actually latched. And even when I know I checked it, the thought comes back in like, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?”

I know that probably sounds a bit extreme, but that’s the part I’m trying to make stop.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are driven by a need for things to be symmetrical or exact?

Not really symmetrical, no. I don’t think it’s about things matching or being exact in that way.

It’s more… I’ll reopen a file, reread an email, check the online payment confirmation again, just to make sure I didn’t miss something. And sometimes I’ll kind of repeat the figures silently in my head until they feel settled, which I know probably sounds a little odd.

It can make something simple, like an invoice or a logo revision, take much longer than it should — sometimes hours I can’t really bill for. But it doesn’t feel like symmetry so much as needing to be sure. Does that answer what you mean?
Is your need to repeat these checks more about being in control of the situation or about avoiding a potential mistake?

I think it’s more about avoiding a potential mistake, yes. I mean, I suppose there’s a feeling of wanting control in there somewhere, but what brings me in is really these doubts that I’ve missed something important.

Like a number on the mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof, or whether a door was actually latched. And even when I know I’ve checked, the thought kind of barges back in — “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” It sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but that’s honestly what it feels like. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like the thoughts that lead you to repeat these checks are more intrusive and unwanted, or are they more about a deliberate attempt to prevent something bad from happening?

They feel intrusive, yes. I mean, I do end up checking because I’m trying to prevent something bad, but the thought itself doesn’t feel deliberate.

It’s more like this doubt just barges in — that I’ve missed a number on the mortgage payment, or overlooked something in a client proof, or didn’t really latch the door — even when I know I already checked. And then it turns into, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?”

I know that sounds a bit much, but that’s how it lands in my head. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?

target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that I keep getting these awful doubts that I've missed something important—a number on the mortgage payment, a clause in a client proof, a door not latched—and even when I know I checked it, the thought barges back in like, 'What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?'
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the fear or intrusive doubt driving the repeated checking—whether it is fear of mistakes versus needing things just right—which is most directly about the obsessive thoughts behind the behavior.

patient.answer:
I think it’s more the fear of making a mistake, honestly. Not so much wanting it to be “just right” in a perfect way.

It’s those doubts that keep coming back — like maybe I missed a number on the mortgage payment, or missed something in a client proof, or didn’t latch a door properly. Even if I know I checked, the thought sort of barges back in, like, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything?

That sounds a bit dramatic when I say it, I know. But that’s more what I’m trying to quiet down. Does that make sense?

patient.answer:
Yes… I think that’s right. It’s mostly fear of what could happen if I got something wrong.

I know some of the things sound ordinary — like a number on the mortgage payment, or a line in a client proof, or whether the door is latched — but then this doubt comes back even after I’ve checked. It’s like my mind says, “What if this is the one mistake that causes a serious problem?”

I’m not trying to be difficult or overly fussy, I don’t think. I’m just trying to get rid of that awful feeling that I’ve missed something important. Does that make sense?

doctor.question: When you repeat these checks, is it more about preventing a specific bad outcome from happening or making sure things are done in a very specific way?

target_item.name: Compulsions
target_item.manifestation: I end up reopening files, rereading emails, checking the online payment confirmation, and sometimes saying the figures silently in my head until they feel 'settled,' which can turn a simple invoice or logo revision into hours I can't bill for.

patient.answer:
I think it’s more about preventing something bad from happening, yes… though sometimes it gets mixed up with needing it to feel settled, if that makes sense.

Like with work, I’ll reopen files more than once, reread emails, check the online payment confirmation again. And I might sort of say the figures silently in my head until they feel… okay, or settled. I’m a little embarrassed saying that.

It’s not that I need to do it in some exact special way, I don’t think. It’s more that I’m afraid I’ve missed something, and then I keep checking until the feeling quiets down. Sometimes a simple invoice or logo revision can take hours, which is frustrating because I can’t really bill for all of that. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
